big_idea: We use likelihood words to PREDICT and make INFORMED DECISIONS.
learning_intention: We are learning to use likelihood words to make a prediction.
student_learning_goal: I can use likelihood words to make a prediction.
success_criteria: I can MAKE a prediction with a likelihood word.
I can DECIDE using a likelihood word.
I can REVISE if data changes.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Lucky Lou and Maybe Mae — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Coin and Dice Cards (1 set per pair)

minds_on.hook: Maybe Mae: I'll flip a coin 10 times. PREDICT — how many heads? Use the SCALE! Mae opens: 'PREDICT, then TEST, then TELL!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Maybe Mae the Cat puppet in striped shirt. 'Detective friends — yesterday we placed events on the scale. Today we PREDICT.'

Define. 'A PREDICTION is what we THINK will happen — BEFORE we test.'

Demo. 'I'll flip a coin 10 times. PREDICT how many heads.'

Show choices: 0 (impossible-zone), 1-2 (unlikely), 5 (equally likely), 8-9 (likely), 10 (certain).

Most children pick 5. 'Why 5? Because heads is EQUALLY LIKELY each flip.'

Flip 10 times. Tally on board. Suppose result: 6 heads. 'Was my prediction good? Close — 5 was equally likely, we got 6.'

'Maybe Mae says — predictions use the SCALE. We DECIDE based on the prediction.'

Demo decision. 'If snow is LIKELY tomorrow, we DECIDE to wear boots.'

Show 4 decision scenarios:
- Snow likely → wear boots ✓
- Rain unlikely → leave umbrella?
- Test certain on Friday → study now ✓
- Treat is impossible at school → don't expect it

'Maybe Mae says — every prediction leads to a DECISION.'

Now each pair gets a Coin Card and Dice Card. Round 1 (3 min): pair predicts heads/tails (10 flips) and dice rolls (10 rolls of getting a 6).

'Maybe Mae says — predictions are GUESSES based on likelihood. They can be wrong!'

steps.instruction: Hand out 6 prediction scenarios. Pairs predict each.
For each, write likelihood word + decision.
Stretch: revise prediction with new info.
Help with decision links — likely → do, unlikely → don't.
STRATEGY COMPARE: After pairs predict 2-3 scenarios, pause for share-out. Two pairs explain HOW they decided. Class compares: which uses data more explicitly? Cite Konold (1989).
steps.teacher_prompt: Mae: 'Same data, two predictions — what made each one strong?'

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: word; explanation; decision; revision; consistency.

discussion_prompts: Name a LIKELY event for tomorrow.
When do we REVISE a prediction?
consolidation.exit_routine: Mae's prediction refrain — 'Maybe Mae says — PREDICT, then TEST, then TELL!' (3x). Each child writes one prediction with data citation.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child predicts WITHOUT a likelihood word — repairing the bare-guess trap at Grade 3
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On predict-and-decide, the trap is bare-guess prediction: child predicts without referencing data. Konold (1989) 'outcome approach' frames this — predictions must be data-grounded.

Yesterday Lucky introduced the 5-word scale. Today predictions from data. Lesson 3 two populations; Lesson 4 mean/mode; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Prediction activity. Child writes 'Yes' for 'Will it rain tomorrow?' (no word).
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Maybe Mae asks — which WORD? Likely? Unlikely?'

Guide. 'Look at the sky. Look at the forecast. Pick ONE word — likely, unlikely, certain, equally likely.'

Generalise. 'Maybe Mae says — predictions use the SCALE word, not just yes/no.'

If still bare: provide the frame. 'It is ___ that ___ will happen.'
common_misconceptions: All predictions are 50/50. (Repair: scale has 5 zones.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child predicts without citing data: drill 'use the DATA card — what does it say?'; child re-predicts citing the row.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child cites data but ignores ratio: drill 'BIG section, BIG chance — small section, small chance.'
DIAGNOSTIC C — child predicts but cannot articulate: force sentence frame 'I predict ___ because the data shows ___.'

parts_outline.task: Predict 4 coin/dice scenarios with likelihood words.
For 4 weather/school scenarios, write a prediction + decision.
Revise ONE prediction with new info.
